subject: How to make your script user friendly?

messages.author: 6d516dae6aab4320
messages.subject: How to make your script user friendly?
parts:
Hi all,

Can anyone please refer me (or give some tips) to sources that explain how to make your script user friendly as possible? I wrote a script and my assumption is that the people that will use it don't know R. They will just need to know how to open R and run the script. Therefore I'm trying to make my script user friendly as possible. I'm sure there are general suggestions I can follow. Currently my script contains a few variables that the user assigns a value to and later in the script these variables are used as the arguments for a few functions that I call later on in the script.
Any reference to a source of information will be greatly appreciated.
Best,
Ayala

messages.author: a305e65fa9dfb74d
messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] How to make your script user friendly?
parts:
It seems you are asking about the usability of the script, but I rather start with the readability of the script, and remind everyone of the many style guides out there.
My favorite is Google's:
https://google-styleguide.googlecode.com/svn/trunk/Rguide.xml

Regarding the usability:
Assuming your users are R natives, try and stick to R's natural "flavors":
my.object<- foo(x,y,arg=TRUE, arg2=FALSE,...)
plot(my.object)

If your users are shell natives (bash, csh, ...), a piping flavored interface might be more natural:
library(magrittr)
foo(x,y,arg=TRUE, arg2=FALSE,...) %>% plot

If your users are object oriented natives, they have different taste buds all together:
my.object$foo(x,y,arg=TRUE, arg2=FALSE,...)
my.object$plot()

Jonathan
